text:
Casey Mittelstadt has found a spot in Boston, at least on the score sheet: 7 goals and 12 points in 20 games while playing only 14.4 minutes a night. Two of those goals came in a loss to Montreal on Nov. 12, and his name has started showing up in trade chatter too, with a Heavy.com pitch sending a Mittelstadt-led package to Detroit for Dylan Larkin.

Some of this is real. The Bruins have taken 58.9% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, a measure of who is getting the better chances, and that is 6.9 points better than the team without him. He is also generating more of his own looks than last season.

Some of it is luck. He has 7 goals on 4.59 expected goals, and his 24.1% shooting is far above his usual range of 12.9% to 18.3%. His teammates are also finishing hot with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking pegged him as a setup man last season, 81st percentile among forwards in primary shot assists. The play-driving is the part we'd trust; the goal pace is the part we'd expect to cool.
headline: Mittelstadt is scoring, and the shooting is doing a lot
